I had been working in my garage on a small project wearing my crisp blue mechanic's jumpsuit when I was interrupted by a call from my elder neighbor who had a billing dispute with the power company. He asked if I could check his meter, being that his form had grown wary of this world's gravity.

While recording the reading from amongst the hedges which obscured the meter I heard a loud curse from the walkway near the front of the house. My first thought was that my neighbor had come to help, now needed help, had fallen, and couldn't get up. I burst forth from the shrubbery to see a startled mail delivery girl picking up a pile of dropped mail. Relieved that no one was hurt, I quickly jotted down the last few digits of the reading on my clipboard before they escaped from me on their own.

Seeing this, the femailman looked up to me, cocked her head like so many of the dogs which loathe her do, then scrunched up her face and barked, "Fuckin' report me, I don't give a shit."

This unexpected exchange had me momentarily taken aback. I stared blankly having interrupted my first impulse to help her fetch the fallen mail. Instead I watched her ample tail wag reluctantly while waiting for her to clear my path. Try as I might, nothing uplifting made itself available to say. Silently I followed the femailman across my neighbor's lawn to my home, clipboard in hand, and paused for her to leave my entry way having deposited my letters.

"What the fuck is your problem?!", said her scowling visage as she shouldered past me. I spun about with opened mouth ready to explain that this was my house, but froze as an insidious plan had hatched from the egg of good intentions. Hurriedly I scribbled upon the pad, shaking my head and tisk-tisking loudly. She had turned back towards me so I returned her gaze resolutely while making an emphatic checkmark gesture on the formerly blank "report form".

The femailman huffed and puffed then trotted away briskly, gathering the mail from her pouch for the next house. I followed behind at a safe distance, but was not unseen. A middle finger was thrust my way after having deposited another neighbor's mail. Again I pursed my lips and shook my head in mock disappointment then gave a vigorous check mark and quick jot to my clipboard.

I knew then my neighbor's meter reading would have to wait. It couldn't be helped. I might have to track this rare she-beast all the way down the block and up the other side, observing her fascinating temperament for posterity the whole way. It wouldn't do to depart on bad terms for no good reason, so I would at least make her misunderstood reason a good one.

The journey was perilous but I had the home-field advantage. I weathered many dirty looks and muttered oaths and the occasional silent stand off -- one lasting a full minute before she resumed her migratory pattern. I feared I would be attacked at any moment, but the growing intensity of the slow speed chase was irresistible. My "report form" was overly full by the time we were within a driveway's distance of her femailman mail van, parked just a house further up the block than where we started our adventure. With lightning speed this strange creature spun on her heel and aimed a readied pepper spray directly at me.

"Fuck Off!" she shouted while quaking in what must have been a frightful adrenalin rush and rage.

I ignored her briefly, raised the clip board to block her potential release of defensive spray, and scribbled one final time on my clip board, then yanked the page out cleanly. I calmly folded and creased a short portion at the top of the "form", and tore it off, pocketing the smaller piece.

As if an olive branch of peace I held aloft the chicken scratched page. "I'm letting you off with a warning", I told her, "but don't let it happen again."

The femailman cocked her head again quizzically and I could swear she sniffed the air testing it for danger. Her curiosity must have won out because she cautiously approached and took the proffered letter, sans envelope or postage.

I savored the bewildered expression of her face momentarily, her eyes growing wider as she examined the scribbles and checkmarks surrounding a stick figure portrait of her complete with mailbag, dog ears, tail, fangs, devil's horns, and a pepper shaped cloud billowing from her bum. Before she could say anything I turned and strode as purposefully as possible across the street back to the hedges. "Wubba Lubba Dub Dub!" I shouted to her then disappeared into the shrubs from whence I came.

It was only then I heard her chuckle, then laugh, as the realization of absurdity must have dawned on the confused femailman.

I waited until she drove away before emerging and giving the meter reading portion of the Speech Police Report Form to my neighbor, the elder one.

There's no telling what preposterous conclusions her delivery bound brain must have arrived at to explain the sudden appearance and disappearance of an Official Speech Police Impersonator. One can only hope she searches the meaning of my cryptic parting phrase.

In 9mm I can see deals where HST/XTP/Gold Dot(original) are around 65 cents per pop. Obviously those will perform so the question is, are there any really solid performers that will penetrate well and perform reliably that you can get for significantly cheaper?

For shotguns it seems to me as long as it goes bang, any buckshot or slug will do more of less.
